answer.rationale: The failure mode is concurrent: a release 2h ago, p99 climbing, and heavy peak writes. We cannot afford exploratory work. I will spend the 1 verification on memory_b1 (rolling back a release cleared a checkout error spike and finished without customer impact) because it directly supports the rollback posture under a related prior failure. memory_b6 shows the canary/gating system has surfaced regressions before, consistent with a regression-shaped signature; memory_b2 shows failover is viable as a fallback if rollback does not recover latency, but rollback is first because it preserves writes. Circuit breaker would shed settlement writes, which conflicts with the primary objective of not losing customer writes. Adding capacity takes effect too late to help a 5x p99 spike already in progress. Read replica routing is irrelevant to a write-path regression.
